references.text: God opened Hagar's eyes so that she saw a spring of water, just as the Lord opened Balaam's eyes to see the angel.
Elisha prayed that his servant's eyes might be opened to see the army of the Lord, similar to how Balaam's eyes were opened.
Joshua meets the commander of the Lord's army with a drawn sword and falls on his face in worship, just as Balaam did.
David saw the angel of the Lord with a drawn sword in hand, paralleling Balaam's vision of the angel with a drawn sword.
The opening of eyes is a recurring theme—here Adam and Eve's eyes were opened, contrasting with the spiritual opening of Balaam's eyes.
The eyes of the travelers on the road to Emmaus were opened so that they recognized Jesus, paralleling how the Lord opened Balaam's eyes.
Earlier in the same account, the angel standing on the road with a drawn sword is described as being seen by the donkey but not by Balaam.
